$comment: Licences of what the website is built from and serves, checked on every build by scripts/third-party-licenses.mjs,
which also writes public/third-party-licenses.txt from them. The top level is for npm packages, "python" for the
Python wheels the playground serves. Only permissive licences (and the OFL, for the fonts) are allowed for every
package; anything else is a decision about one package, recorded with its reason.
An entry applies to the package named by its key, or to every package starting with it if it ends in *.
'declared' is the licence exactly as the package states it: if a release states anything else, the entry no
longer applies and the build fails until someone reads the new licence. 'license' replaces a declared licence
that is not SPDX; 'allow' allows more licences for this package only; 'source' is where the source code of the
served version is, for licences that ask the site to say so (MPL-2.0).
'texts' are upstream licence and NOTICE texts the package does not ship, saved in licenses/ from 'from' (where
{version} is the package's version, {python} and {emscripten} Pyodide's). They were saved for 'version': when
the package changes version, the build fails until `npm run vendor-licenses` refetches them, for review.
'notServed' says why a package that ships no licence text needs none here: nothing of it reaches the site.

pagefind.reason: The site's search: pagefind/ (its UI, scripts and WebAssembly) is served. Its npm packages have no licence file.

@pagefind/*.reason: Pagefind's UI (@pagefind/default-ui) and its per-platform indexer, which writes the served pagefind/ files. Same repository and licence as pagefind.

pyodide.reason: The playground's Python runtime, served unmodified from playground/pyodide/: Pyodide (MPL-2.0), CPython compiled to WebAssembly with its standard library (PSF licence and the licences of the software CPython incorporates), and Emscripten's runtime and C library (MIT, and musl's MIT licence). The npm package ships none of these texts. MPL-2.0 asks a distributor of the executable form to say where its source is: "source".

@img/sharp-libvips-*.notServed: libvips, the native image library sharp uses to resize images while the site is built; it runs on the build machine and none of it is served.
@img/sharp-libvips-*.reason: Build tool only, dynamically linked by sharp, unmodified: the LGPL puts no obligation on the site.

@img/sharp-wasm32.reason: sharp compiled to WebAssembly with libvips, a fallback for platforms without a native build. Build tool only; none of it is served.

lightningcss.reason: The CSS minifier of the build. Its output is the site's own CSS, not its code, and MPL-2.0 binds only changes to its own files.

lightningcss-*.reason: lightningcss's per-platform native binary. Build tool only.

@astrojs/compiler-binding-*.notServed: The native Astro compiler, which turns the site's .astro files into HTML while it is built.

@bruits/satteri-*.notServed: A native Markdown processor used while the site is built.

@rolldown/binding-*.notServed: The native bundler (Rolldown) of the build.

@napi-rs/wasm-runtime.notServed: Loads the build tools' WebAssembly fallbacks on the build machine.

@vscode/l10n.notServed: Used by the type checker (astro check) on the build machine.

am-i-vibing.notServed: Used by Astro's command line to detect the terminal it runs in.

process-ancestry.notServed: Used by am-i-vibing in Astro's command line.

piccolore.notServed: Colours the output of Astro's command line.

boolbase.notServed: Used by CSS selector matching while pages are built (svgo, Starlight).

python.$comment: The wheels the playground serves (public/playground/), as Pyodide builds them. Names are matched as PyPI normalizes them.

pandas.reason: Pyodide's pandas wheel ships only pandas' own LICENSE, not the licences of the code pandas bundles and compiles in (LICENSES/ in its repository and in its PyPI wheels).

pyarrow.reason: Pyodide's pyarrow wheel ships no licence and no NOTICE; Apache-2.0 requires both to go with every copy. They are Apache Arrow's, at the same version.

pyodide-unix-timezones.reason: Ships no licence file. Its repository has no tags, so the text is from its main branch.

python-dateutil.reason: Its LICENSE puts contributions since 2017-12-01 under Apache-2.0 and the earlier code under BSD-3-Clause, so both apply.
